nodes.label: Application (search or RAG service)
nodes.summary: Sends a query (already embedded, or text to embed) with k and an optional metadata filter, and uses the nearest items.

nodes.label: Embedding model service
nodes.summary: Turns text or images into vectors. The same model must be used for stored items and queries; changing it changes every vector.

nodes.label: Source of truth
nodes.summary: The catalogue, documents or media whose items are indexed. Owns ids and metadata.

nodes.label: Query coordinator
nodes.summary: Fans each query out to the shards (or a chosen subset), applies timeouts and replica retries, merges the per-shard top-K lists and returns the result. The Taobao example in the DiskANN paper routes queries to all shards and aggregates.

nodes.label: Index shard (replica set)
nodes.summary: Holds one partition of the vectors with an ANN index and answers top-K queries for it. Replicated for availability and throughput (replication is our design).

nodes.label: Graph index (HNSW or Vamana)
nodes.summary: Proximity graph searched greedily. HNSW has layers chosen with exponentially decaying probability and logarithmic search scaling; DiskANN's Vamana graph is searched with a beam of W candidates.

nodes.label: Compressed vectors (product quantization)
nodes.summary: Short codes (for example 32 bytes per point) kept in memory to compute approximate distances. Lossy: compression-based indexes alone reach about 0.5 1-recall@1 in the DiskANN paper.

nodes.label: Full vectors and graph on SSD (DiskANN)
nodes.summary: The graph and full-precision vectors are stored on the SSD, so a billion points fit on one machine with 64 GB of RAM. Beam search batches reads to limit round trips.

nodes.label: Filter predicate
nodes.summary: Checks each candidate against a search-time criterion; Faiss supports a predicate on ids but does not store arbitrary metadata, so richer filters need a metadata lookup or packed id bits.

nodes.label: Fresh-writes index
nodes.summary: Small in-memory index of recent vectors, searched alongside the shards; deletes are tombstones until consolidation. FreshDiskANN describes this shape: a short-term in-memory index merged into a long-term SSD index by a background StreamingMerge, with lazy deletes in a DeleteList.

nodes.label: Index builder
nodes.summary: Batch job that builds index segments from the vectors, for example clustering the data, building graphs per cluster and merging them as DiskANN does.

nodes.label: Index segments (object storage)
nodes.summary: Built index segments that shards load. A new embedding model gets a new set built beside the old one.

nodes.label: Alternative: blue/green index for a new embedding model
nodes.summary: Build a full new index with the new model, check recall on a labelled query set, switch traffic, keep the old one for rollback.

steps.caption: The query text is embedded with the same model used for the stored items.
The query vector, k and a metadata filter go to the coordinator.
The coordinator sends the query to every shard (one replica each).
The shard walks its graph, using in-memory compressed codes for approximate distances.
For a disk-resident index it reads the neighbourhoods of a few candidates in one batch.
Each candidate is checked against the filter.
The coordinator also searches the fresh-writes index and merges all lists into the final top-K.
A new or changed item is sent to the embedding model.
The vector goes into the small fresh-writes index, searchable at once.
It is also queued for the next periodic build.
The builder writes new index segments.
Shards load the segments; the fresh-writes index can then drop those vectors.

flows.name: A shard is slow or unavailable (failure)

steps.caption: The coordinator's request to one shard times out.
It retries on another replica; if none answers in time it must choose between failing and returning results without that shard's partition (our design reasoning).
With a healthy replica, the shard's top-K arrives and the merge proceeds.
